text:
alex: Seeing a spike in structured-tool validation rejects in eu-west-1 on the fncall path. Console shows fallbacks to 'degen' but billing still charges full. Anyone else noticing this? @mira @jon
mira: Yup, noticed around 10:23. Reject rate jumped to ~3.2% (was ~0.2% last week). Logs show ValidatorError: missing 'items' field in tool_response.
jon: Are these hard rejects or soft? Routing policy should ideally try permissive branch before falling back.
alex: Good question. Runtime is labeling them HARD_REJECT and immediately routing to compact variant; billing_tag remains original_route — that’s what's causing quota misattribution.
sam: Quick idea: either set billing_tag to final_route (post-routing) OR add a reject_reason dimension so we don't bill full for parser-only failures. Tradeoffs: retroactive accounting complexity and reporting fallout.
emily: From console UX side: users see "fallback used" with no reason. We should surface the reject reason + a sampled example in the per-route dashboard (PII-safe sampling).
mira: Telemetry needs: fncall.validation.reject_count_by_reason + route_before + route_after tags. Also add latency histograms comparing fallback vs original.
alex: +1. Proposal: implement billing_tag update in routing layer and add metric tags. Put behind feature flag fncall_reject_billing_fix for a canary.
jon: Rollout plan sketch: infra change (billing tag) + console tile + new metrics + feature flag. Owner: alex. ETA: PR by EOD, canary next Tue.
sam: Nit: ensure sampling strips PII and we store just schema-diff or anonymized example, not raw user payload.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: staging build #789 -> running unit tests.
ops-bot: FYI, this spike raised alerts but stayed low-sev, paging not triggered.
alex: Adding pasted example from logs to illustrate:
```
ValidatorError: missing_required_field items
route_before: model-a-v1
route_after: model-a-compact
billing_tag: model-a-v1
```
mira: I'll add a dashboard tile in console: "Fncall validation rejects" with reason breakdown + link to runbook.
jon: Runbook addition: if reject_rate > 1% AND fallback_ratio > 30% then escalate to oncall and pause canary.
emily: Also update API docs to clarify which rejects are billable and when fallbacks are charged. Add changelog entry.
alex: Thanks all — I'll open the PR and add the feature-flag. Will drop the link here when it's up.
sam: :thumbsup:
